Winchester's population increased by around 10,900 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 130,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Winchester increased by 9.3%, from just under 116,600 in 2011 to around 127,400 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Winchester was home to around 1.4 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 1.3 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Winchester than across the South East

Median age in Winchester

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Winchester increased by one year, from 42 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 3,000 (an increase of 13.4%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,100 (4.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.7 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Unpaid care in Winchester

Winchester saw the South East's joint largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 7.9% in 2011 to 4.7% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Every local authority area across the South East saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.3% to 4.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Winchester decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Winchester (3.5 percentage points) than in nearby East Hampshire (1.4 percentage points).

In Winchester, the percentage of private renting increased from 14.1% in 2011 to 17.6% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby East Hampshire increased from 11.7% to 13.0%.

The rate of social renting in Winchester fell from 15.5% to 15.3%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 67.5% to 65.6%.

Private renting in Winchester increased by 3.5 percentage points

Religion in Winchester

In 2021, 42.2% of Winchester residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.3% in 2011. The rise of 14.9 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Winchester. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 48.6% of people in Winchester described themselves as Christian (down from 63.2%), while 6.3% did not state their religion (down from 7.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 42.2% of usual residents in Winchester reported having "No religion"

Winchester residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 109,100 Winchester residents said they were born in England. This represented 85.6% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 101,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 87.3% of Winchester's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just under 2,100 Winchester residents reporting this country of birth (1.6%). This figure was down from around 2,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.9% of the population of Winchester.

The number of Winchester residents born in Wales remained close to 1,700 between the last two census (from 1.5% of the local population in 2011 to 1.3% in 2021)

In 2021, 85.6% of Winchester residents reported their country of birth as England

Health in Winchester

In 2021, 53.6% of Winchester residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 52.5% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 33.3% to 33.1%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Winchester residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.7%, while those describing their health as "bad" was 2.6% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Winchester decreased by 0.2 percentage points

National identity in Winchester

In 2021, 5.6% of Winchester residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 4.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 50 people (2.2%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Winchester that identified as "British only" increased from 18.9% to 59.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%) than in Winchester (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Winchester increased by 1.3 percentage points

Family in Winchester

Of Winchester households, 19.2% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 20.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.5%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.3% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 5.5% to 6.0%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Winchester (1.7 percentage points) than across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Winchester decreased by 1.7 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Winchester residents aged 16 years and over, 33.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 30.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (50.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 52.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Winchester that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 8.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Winchester (3.2 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Winchester increased by 3.2 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Winchester residents aged 16 years and over, 55.6% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 57.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.0% in 2011. The percentage of retired Winchester residents increased from 23.2% to 24.1%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Winchester (1.7 percentage points) than across the South East (1.3 percentage points, from 59.0% to 57.6%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Winchester decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Winchester stood out from other areas for working hours

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week fell in Winchester, but rose across the South East.

In Winchester, the percentage that worked 15 hours or less in a week fell from 12.9% in 2011 to 12.5% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 10.4% to 11.0%.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Winchester fell from 17.3% to 14.3%, while the percentage of adults in employment who worked 31 to 48 hours increased from 51.4% to 54.4%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Winchester decreased by 0.4 percentage points

Disability in Winchester

In 2021, 5.1% of Winchester residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.8%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.7% in 2011. The proportion of Winchester residents who were not disabled decreased from 85.4% to 85.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%) than in Winchester (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Winchester decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Winchester

In 2021, 3.1% of Winchester residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 2.3% in 2011. The 0.8 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 93.6% of people in Winchester identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 95.7% in 2011), while 2.0% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.3% in 2011 to 0.7% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
